stops.name: Jackson Square
stops.teaser: A parade ground with a man on a rearing horse.
stops.map: Jackson Square, 700 Decatur St, New Orleans, LA
stops.clue: In the French Quarter, find the park with a bronze statue of a rider on a rearing horse, in front of a big church.
stops.safety: The square is crowded with performers and tourists. Watch your belongings, the uneven sidewalks and the heat.

q.hint: The square is named for him.
q.verify: The square is named for Andrew Jackson, whose statue was erected in 1851 (National Park Service). Written from sources, not yet checked on site.

now.head: Today
now.label: The square today
now.line: Jackson Square in the French Quarter. Photo from 2008.

story: In the 19th century the square was the Place d'Armes, the traditional site of important ceremonies and parades.

On December 18, 1814, Andrew Jackson reviewed about 6,000 troops there. His speech, translated by Edward Livingston, urged unity against a common enemy. The Americans then won the Battle of New Orleans.
The square kept the Place d'Armes name until 1851, when the current Andrew Jackson statue was erected and it became Jackson Square. It is a National Historic Landmark.
stops.fact: Jackson used the square to muster troops before the Battle of New Orleans.
stops.disputed: Nothing big is disputed here. The mistake is thinking the square always had Jackson's name.

claims.t: Jackson Square was originally called the Place d'Armes.
claims.why: The National Park Service: it kept that name until 1851.

claims.t: Jackson Square was named for Andrew Jackson from the day it was laid out.
claims.why: It was the Place d'Armes until the statue was erected in 1851.

spot.q: Until 1851 this square had a different name. What was it?
spot.why: The square kept the Place d'Armes name until 1851, when the Andrew Jackson statue was erected and it became Jackson Square.

stops.teaser: A church rebuilt after a Good Friday fire.
stops.map: St. Louis Cathedral, 615 Pere Antoine Alley, New Orleans, LA
stops.clue: Stand in Jackson Square and face the big white church with tall spires.
stops.safety: Respect worship times and quiet inside. Watch for crowds and carriage traffic around the square.

now.label: Inside the cathedral

story: The first church on the site, a crude wooden building, went up in 1718. A brick and timber church was completed in 1727. The Great New Orleans Fire destroyed it on Good Friday, March 21, 1788.

The third church was begun in 1789 and finished in 1794, and the church became a cathedral in 1793. The present building dates mostly to 1850. A central tower designed by Benjamin Henry Latrobe in 1819 collapsed in 1850 during rebuilding.

Pope Paul VI named it a minor basilica in 1964. Wikipedia calls it "the oldest cathedral in continuous use in the United States," a title it shares with the Royal Presidio Chapel in Monterey, California.
stops.fact: The 1788 fire destroyed the earlier church and many other buildings.
stops.disputed: The "oldest cathedral" title is shared with a chapel in Monterey, California, so it depends on how you count.

claims.t: The Great New Orleans Fire of 1788 destroyed the earlier church on this site.
claims.why: Wikipedia: it burned on Good Friday, March 21, 1788.

claims.t: St. Louis Cathedral is the only oldest cathedral in continuous use in the United States.
claims.why: Wikipedia says it shares the distinction with the Royal Presidio Chapel in Monterey, California.

spot.q: Benjamin Henry Latrobe designed a central tower for the cathedral in 1819. What happened to it?
spot.why: The central tower designed by Latrobe in 1819 collapsed in 1850 during rebuilding. The present building dates mostly to 1850.

stops.map: The Cabildo, 701 Chartres St, New Orleans, LA
stops.clue: Next to the cathedral on Jackson Square, find the pale, arched building with a dark sloped roof.

story: The Cabildo was built between 1795 and 1799 as the home of Spanish municipal government in New Orleans. Gilberto Guillemard is listed as its architect. Spanish officials used its courtroom from 1799 to 1803.
Ceremonies marking the transfer of Louisiana took place at the Cabildo in late 1803. A third floor with a French-style mansard roof was added in 1847.
A fire on May 11, 1988 destroyed the cupola and the entire third floor. The building reopened in 1994 after restoration. Since 1911 it has housed the Louisiana State Museum.
stops.fact: The Sala Capitular hosted landmark court cases, including Plessy v. Ferguson.
stops.disputed: Nothing big is disputed here. The mistake is assuming the roof you see is original.

claims.t: The Cabildo was built in the 1790s as the home of Spanish city government.
The mansard roof on the Cabildo is original from the 1790s.
claims.why: The third floor and mansard roof were added in 1847, then rebuilt after the 1988 fire.

stops.name: French Market
stops.teaser: A market older than the country around it.
stops.map: French Market, 1008 N Peters St, New Orleans, LA
stops.clue: Walk along the river side of the Quarter to the long covered market. At its upriver end you will find a famous café.
stops.safety: The market is crowded and the streets around it are busy. Watch for traffic and wet pavement.
stops.field: Field notes pending: nobody has walked this stop for the app yet.

q.verify: Wikipedia says the market marks the upriver end at Café du Monde. Confirm on site. Written from sources, not yet checked on site.

now.head: Today
now.label: The market hall today
now.line: A covered hall of the French Market. Photo from 2016.

story: Part of the space was dedicated as a market in 1791, during the colonial period. Wikipedia says it began as a Native American trading post before European colonization, with no date given. The oldest surviving structures date to about 1813.
The Works Progress Administration made major renovations in the 1930s. The market spans six blocks, from Café du Monde to the flea market stalls across from the New Orleans Mint.
Wikipedia calls it "the oldest of its kind in the United States."
stops.fact: The market began where Café du Monde now stands.
stops.disputed: "Oldest" is argued. Other markets also claim long histories, and counts depend on what you mean by "public market."

claims.t: The French Market was dedicated as a market in 1791.
claims.why: Wikipedia: part of the space was dedicated as a market in 1791.

claims.t: The French Market is the oldest public market in the United States.
claims.why: Wikipedia says so, but other markets claim long histories, so the claim depends on definitions.

spot.q: How many blocks does the French Market span?
spot.why: The market spans six blocks, from Cafe du Monde to the flea market stalls across from the New Orleans Mint.
